question: Under the PC and PNDT Act 1994, communicating the sex of the foetus to the pregnant woman or her family is prohibited even when the sex is determined incidentally during a medically indicated anomaly scan.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. The PCPNDT Act prohibits communication of foetal sex in any form — verbal, written, or non-verbal — regardless of the reason for the scan. An accidental disclosure during a routine anomaly scan carries the same legal consequence as a deliberate one.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The Act's prohibition on communicating foetal sex is absolute — it applies regardless of how the sex was determined (incidentally or deliberately) and regardless of the clinical context. The sonologist must not disclose the sex even if asked by the woman herself.
